definition: A hierarchical control system (HCS) is a form of control system in which a set of devices and governing software is arranged in a hierarchical tree.
details: When the links in the tree are implemented by a computer network, then that hierarchical control system is also a form of networked control system.
story: Picture guardrails on a mountain road — not there to slow you down on the straightaways, but to keep you from flying off the cliff. Boil it down and it is this: A hierarchical control system (HCS) is a form of control system in which a set of devices and governing software is arranged in a hierarchical tree. Here is why it matters: When the links in the tree are implemented by a computer network, then that hierarchical control system is also a form of networked control system. It is the difference between “it works” and “it is safe to put in front of people.” That deliberate caution is Hierarchical control system.
